cognize

KOG-nyze · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To cognize is to become aware of, perceive, or come to know something through mental effort.

It took the jury several long minutes to fully cognize the significance of the forensic report the lawyer had just read aloud.

Example

Long before he could speak in full sentences, the toddler could already cognize the difference between his mother's footsteps and a stranger's.

Cognizing something doesn't require language at all -- it's the basic mental act of perceiving and registering that something is true or present.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

perceive: To perceive something is to take it in through the senses -- a sound, a color, a movement registers on you. To cognize adds a layer of mental work: the mind actively registers what the thing is and that it is really there. Perceiving is sensing; cognizing is effortful mental awareness.

apprehend: To apprehend an idea is to get a first mental hold on it -- you grasp its outline before you could ever explain it fully. To cognize is the broader act of becoming aware of something through deliberate mental effort, whether or not understanding follows. Apprehending begins to understand; cognizing simply registers.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

overlook: to fail to notice or register something

disregard: to choose not to think about or consider something

Where it sits · how deep the mental grasp goes

notice → cognize → comprehend

notice vs. cognize: To notice something is simply to register that it exists, a much lighter mental action than fully cognizing it.

comprehend vs. cognize: To comprehend something is to understand it completely and deeply, a fuller mental grasp than simply cognizing it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — co-: together, thoroughly (an intensifying prefix) (Latin)

root — gnize: to know (Latin gnoscere, 'to know')

Put it together: Cognize combines co- ('together,' an intensifying prefix) with gnize (from Latin gnoscere, 'to know') -- literally 'to come to know fully,' which is exactly what cognize means: to become aware of or mentally grasp something.

Use the root in a new word: recognize: The new badge scanner refused to recognize half the students on Monday morning.

Word Choice

Cognize is a formal, rather academic word -- you'll see it mostly in philosophy, psychology, or careful analytical writing, not in everyday conversation.
